analysis:
Examined docs/threat-model.yaml head lines 470–1394 against the canonical index and supplied T-041 definition. These excerpts are unchanged according to the complete range map. They retain fail-closed response encryption, bounded cancellation, process-scoped keys, legacy/App Attest separation, final-handoff authorization, privileged-helper isolation, and authenticated cache scoping. Existing GPU-memory, weight-verification, cache timing, detached-media retention and replay limitations are not PR regressions.
The only mapped edit is docs/threat-model.yaml:1969–1970: media-ingestion documentation adds video/x-m4v and video/mov aliases while requiring MP4/QuickTime bytes and retaining external-reference restrictions and resource caps. This does not itself demonstrate a weakened control or an unmodeled threat. Integration must verify the corresponding media-ingestion changes against T-050/A-001: aliases must preserve byte/container validation, AVURLAssetReferenceRestrictions.forbidAll, in-memory handling, and decoded-byte/duration/frame/video-count/aggregate limits. Those implementations are not supplied in these units, so their enforcement remains unverified rather than an observed vulnerability. No supported finding arises from the reviewed excerpts; this is not clearance of the implementation change or unchanged dependencies.
